data.title: Yidu Tech Posts RMB 61.3 Million in Profit, Sustaining Growth Momentum in H1 FY2027
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Yidu Tech (2158.HK), a leading Hong Kong-listed healthcare AI company, held its FY2027 interim results briefing this morning, presenting its operating performance for the six months ended September 30, 2026.

Yidu Tech remained profitable during the reporting period, recording profit for the period of RMB 61.31 million and profit attributable to owners of the parent of RMB 56.55 million. First-half profit reached nearly 80% of the RMB 78.77 million recorded for the full FY2026. New orders in the AI for Medical segment rose 98% year on year. Adjusted EBITDA increased 106% year on year to RMB 111 million, while operating expenses as a percentage of revenue fell from 61% to 51.8%, reflecting improved operating efficiency.

"Healthcare AI is at a pivotal stage, moving from validating the technology to proving its value in practice," said Xu Jiming, Co-Founder and CEO of Yidu Tech. "Over the past decade, we have built lasting competitive advantages through healthcare data, disease knowledge and experience in real-world settings. Our priority now is to turn these capabilities into products and platforms that can be deployed at scale. By embedding AI in core workflows across healthcare delivery, pharmaceuticals, insurance and patient services, we aim to make it part of the infrastructure that improves the quality and efficiency of healthcare."

"These results build on our first full year of profitability and point to a structural improvement in the quality of our earnings," said Feng Xiaoying, Executive Director and CFO of Yidu Tech. "We are entering a new phase focused on efficiency and the quality of growth. We will direct more resources toward core businesses with high barriers to entry, key customers with strong retention, and platform capabilities that benefit from network effects. Return on invested capital and customer lifetime value will guide those decisions as we pursue resilient, sustainable earnings growth."

YiduCore Brings Together Data, Algorithms and Real-World Applications

YiduCore, Yidu Tech's core algorithm engine, is an integrated healthcare AI system built on more than a decade of experience in real-world healthcare settings. Data improves the algorithms, the algorithms power applications, and those applications generate data that feeds back into the system. This cycle allows Yidu Tech to refine its AI capabilities and reuse them across applications.

Drawing on its long-standing work with healthcare institutions, Yidu Tech continues to advance healthcare data governance and the way it organizes disease knowledge. According to company data, its technology system covers more than 12,000 healthcare institutions. On that foundation, the company has built a data framework spanning 103 diseases and continues to expand its medical terminology and disease knowledge resources to support model training and specialized applications.

The company continues to train and refine healthcare-specific large language models, improving their ability to handle ultra-long contexts, interpret medical knowledge and perform complex reasoning. It is also expanding its medical evidence base to support evidence-based clinical questions, literature searches and traceability to original sources.

Yidu Tech has developed more than 400 specialty-specific AI agents for clinical care, research and hospital management. In one hospital, 80% to 91.5% of the content generated by an AI agent for discharge summaries was accepted in routine use.

Three Business Segments Expand the Commercial Use of AI

During the reporting period, Yidu Tech focused on its core businesses and used YiduCore as a shared technology foundation to extend its AI capabilities across healthcare delivery, pharmaceuticals, insurance and patient services. The company continued to develop its business portfolio and expand the commercial use of its AI solutions.

AI for Medical provides digital and AI-enabled solutions to healthcare institutions at all levels and to government regulators. New orders in the segment rose 98% year on year during the reporting period. The company focused on building high-quality data infrastructure, applying AI to core healthcare workflows and expanding collaboration across the sector. It upgraded YiduEywa to version 6.0 and launched a medical dataset refinement platform to improve the quality of data available for large language model applications. Its shared AI middleware platform, Doctor Copilot, Yidu Evidence and specialty AI agents helped extend the use of AI across clinical care, medical research and hospital management. The company also expanded partnerships in regional healthcare and public health, supporting deployment across institutions and regions. By the end of the reporting period, Yidu Tech had served 141 leading hospitals in China and 53 regulators and policymakers.

AI for Life Sciences provides AI-enabled services across the pharmaceutical R&D and commercialization lifecycle. Segment revenue grew 9.1% year on year during the reporting period. The company continued to integrate AI into its professional services for drug development, clinical research and real-world evidence generation. The Company serves 16 of the world's top 20 multinational pharmaceutical companies. To date, it has participated in or completed at least 552 clinical research projects and undertaken more than 330 prospective and retrospective real-world studies. Drawing on its experience with major pharmaceutical companies, Yidu Tech continues to expand the use of AI throughout drug development and clinical research to deliver higher-value services.

AI for Care, the company's health management platforms and solutions segment, focuses on Supplementary Insurance, chronic disease management and digital health services. Segment revenue grew 4.2% year on year during the reporting period. Yidu Tech has served as the primary operating platform for Beijing Supplementary Insurance for six consecutive years and for Shenzhen Supplementary Insurance for four consecutive years, using its digital operations capabilities to connect insurance coverage, medical services and health management. The company also continued to bring digital therapeutics for diabetes into primary care, expanding the service model to Beijing, Tianjin and Shanxi.

Yidu Tech's FY2027 interim results show sustained profitability and improved operating efficiency as the company turns years of technology development into value in real-world settings. As AI healthcare moves beyond proof of concept and becomes embedded in clinical decision-making, drug development and health management, it can change how those workflows operate across the healthcare system. With continued advances in YiduCore and growing network effects across its three business segments, Yidu Tech aims to make AI an integral part of healthcare operations and build sustainable growth in a trillion-yuan healthcare market.

SOURCE Yidu Tech

data.title: Tata Steel to Buy Stake in Indian Steel Tubes Maker in Near $1.7 Billion Deal
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

Tata Steel agreed Monday to buy a 26.6% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for $1.67 billion, paving the way to take control of the smaller Indian steel tubes maker.

Tata Steel will pay 2,100 Indian rupees, equivalent to $22.67, a share for the stake held by APL Apollo's promoters, the steelmaker said in an exchange filing Monday.

Tata Steel will also make an open offer for a further 26% stake at 2,301.40 rupees a share.

On Sunday, Tata Steel agreed to sell its steel tubes business and its coated steel unit, Tata Steel Colors, to APL Apollo for 280 billion rupees.

APL Apollo would fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalization to de-risk the balance sheet, the statement said.

After the deal closes, APL Apollo will become Tata Steel's main vehicle for growth in steel tubes and coated steel, with a combined capacity of 7.5 million tons a year.

Tata Steel shares are trading 5.8% lower and APL Apollo is down 15%.

data.title: The First Saudi Girl to Speak on a UN Stage with 51Talk Brings Riyadh's Green Vision to COP31
data.description:
A Saudi student speaks at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, as 51Talk marks its fourth consecutive year of bringing Saudi children to UN climate conferences.

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Saudi student Nada Al-Mughairi, 12, took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share how her city's greening efforts inspired her vision for a more sustainable future.

Speaking in English alongside young participants from six countries, Nada delivered a speech on Riyadh's urban greening efforts, a theme closely connected to the Kingdom's Green Riyadh Program and Saudi Green Initiative under Vision 2030.

Nada's participation marks the fourth consecutive year that a Saudi student has joined 51Talk's young delegation at a UN climate conference, following COP28 in Dubai, COP29 in Baku, and COP30 in Belém.

A Young Speaker for a Greener Riyadh

Nada earned her place at COP31 by winning a speaking competition organized by 51Talk in Saudi Arabia. In her speech, she described how new parks, tree-lined streets, and green spaces are transforming Riyadh, and why sustaining them in a desert climate matters to children of her generation.

"Real sustainability is not only about creating something green today. It is about making sure it can survive tomorrow," Nada said.

"We, the younger generation, are not only asking leaders to protect our future. We are ready to help build it," she added.

"When I stood on that stage, I felt I was speaking for every child in Riyadh. Meeting friends from so many countries showed me that we all want the same thing: a greener home for the future," Nada said.

Beyond the stage, Nada met young speakers from Türkiye, Kuwait, Thailand, Indonesia, and China, exchanging ideas about how children in different countries experience climate change.

Turning English into a Voice for Change

51Talk helps children build practical communication skills through personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers.

To further support practical communication skills, 51Talk has introduced انجليزي مصمم للسعوديين (Global Communicator) in Saudi Arabia, a new English curriculum designed to connect language learning with real-world communication. Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, the curriculum features stories, characters, and everyday scenarios rooted in Saudi culture, helping children learn English through familiar places, traditions, and situations.

Through immersive, task-based activities, children practice expressing opinions, solving problems, and communicating with confidence. AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help tailor lessons to each child's needs and make progress more visible to families.

data.title: Singapore's core inflation rate rises to 1.5% in October, below forecast
data.description:
Singapore's key consumer price gauge rose 1.5% in October from a year earlier, official data showed on Monday.

The core inflation rate, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, was lower than the median forecast of 1.7% in a Reuters poll and September's reading of 2%.

Headline inflation was 1.9% in annual terms in October, matching the poll forecast.

The central bank kept its monetary policy unchanged in October, in a move that surprised analysts, with inflation risks expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.

In August, the trade ministry raised its growth forecast for 2026 to a range of 4.5% to 5.5%, from the previous 2.0% to 4.0%.

data.title: Singapore Inflation Slowed in October as Electricity Tariffs Fall
data.description:
By Amanda Lee

SINGAPORE--Singapore's inflation slowed in October, helped by lower household electricity tariffs.

The consumer-price index rose 1.9% from a year earlier, government data showed Monday, down from 2.2% in September. The increase matched the forecast of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.

Consumer prices fell 0.3% from the previous month.

Core inflation, which excludes accommodation and private-transport costs, slowed to 1.5% from 2.0% in September. Economists in the Journal's poll had expected 1.6%.

Household electricity tariffs are 10.4% lower in the fourth quarter from the previous quarter, reflecting lower energy costs.

ANZ's head of Asia Research Khoon Goh said in a recent report that higher public transport fares and an expected increase in electricity prices from January 2027 would likely push core inflation back above 2% in the first quarter.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore has no explicit inflation target. It considers average core inflation of just under 2% consistent with price stability.

"At this stage, with inflation expected to remain within the MAS' forecast range, we see monetary policy staying on hold," Goh said.

He said the central bank could tighten monetary policy in 2027 if prices rise faster than expected.

data.title: India factory demand offsets weaker services growth in November, PMI shows
data.description:
India's private sector activity grew a touch faster in November than the previous month as stronger factory demand and production offset a weaker services expansion, a business survey showed.

  • HSBC's Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, edged up to 56.3 this month from October's 56.2, its highest since June. But growth remained weaker than in the first half of the year, pointing to a modest recovery rather than a strong rebound. A level above 50 indicates expansion.

  • The manufacturing PMI rose to a nine-month high of 56.0 from 54.7, supported by stronger orders, production and hiring. But services PMI slipped to 55.3 from 55.8 with growth in new business unchanged from October.

  • The divergence was sharper in employment. Factories recruited additional staff at the fastest pace in seven months but services firms trimmed jobs for the first time in nearly a year.

  • That uneven expansion is broadly consistent with a Reuters poll pointing to slower economic growth this quarter, following an expected strong performance in July-September, as earlier tax-cut benefits fade and higher borrowing costs weigh on spending.

  • Cost pressures, according to November's PMI, remained mild even as companies raised selling prices faster, contrasting with the broader energy and food inflation pressures noted in the Reuters poll.

  • Companies were more optimistic about the year ahead although confidence remained below its long-run average.

data.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds turned lower on Monday, unable to hold on to opening gains triggered by a US Treasury rally, as traders booked profits after last week's run, and as the rupee plunged sharply.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield was at 7.2185% as of 10:30 a.m. IST, after closing at 7.1868% on Friday. Earlier in the day, it had hit a low of 7.1678%. Indian debt markets will be closed on Tuesday for a local holiday.

Last week, the 10-year bond yield had dropped 12 basis points, mainly tracking lower US yields and a rally in the rupee against the US dollar.

"Bond bulls had already turned cautious as benchmark yield neared the 7.15% handle, but the reversal in rupee allowed profit booking to take over, pushing yield above 7.20%," a trader with a primary dealership said.

The Indian rupee fell sharply and was on its way to touch the 93 per US dollar mark after briefly rising above 92.50 briefly and after closing at 92.67 on Friday.

Bonds started the day with gains after US Treasury yields tumbled on Friday as investors sought safety from equities, with the benchmark 10-year yield posting its biggest weekly drop since early April 2025.

The 10-year yield hovered around 4.90% in Asian trading, amid growth expectations of a more measured Fed stance in December also eased fears of an outsized rate hike.

Brent crude held near $92 a barrel, supported by concerns over escalating US-Iran tensions and positioning ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday.

Persistently high oil prices pose risks for major importer India, threatening to widen its current account deficit, weaken the rupee and fuel inflation.

Investors will now focus on the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision due on December 4, where a majority of economists surveyed by Reuters expect the central bank to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates were trading lower, as receiving interest in the longer end helped.

The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate and the two-year rate (INR2YIBROIS=CC) were not yet traded after ending at 6.47%, and 6.43%. The more liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate was lower at 6.43%.

data.title: Brookfield to acquire India's PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion
data.description:
Brookfield Asset Management said on Monday it has agreed to acquire Indian glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion.

PGP Glass manufactures glass packaging for cosmetics, fragrances, spirits, food and pharmaceutical products.

“We welcome Brookfield and look forward to working with them to accelerate our next phase of growth and value creation," PGP Glass CEO Vijay Shah said.

PGP Glass has 13 furnaces and a production capacity of more than 1,800 tonnes per day, according to its website. It operates across markets including Brazil, India, and the UK.

New York-based Brookfield Asset Management manages more than $1 trillion across asset classes including infrastructure, renewable power, private equity, real estate and credit.

data.title: Asian markets extend losses after Wall Street selloff; U.S. futures rebound
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded mostly lower on Monday, extending last week's global technology-led selloff as concerns over AI valuations continued to weigh on investor sentiment. South Korea's Kospi bore the brunt of the selling, falling more than 5%, even as U.S. equity futures rebounded following Wall Street's steep weekly losses. Japan's markets remained closed for a public holiday.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 0.64%, China’s Shanghai Composite slipped 0.96%, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged down 0.20%, while India’s Sensex lost 0.47%.

China’s state-backed funds invested a record 90B yuan ($13.5B) in ETFs on Friday, stepping up efforts to support the country’s stock market as a prolonged selloff pushed the benchmark CSI 300 Index into bear-market territory.

Australia's composite PMI falls to the lowest level in over five years.

Spot gold rebounded around 1.7% to $3,584 an ounce, recovering after a sharp 8.9% decline last week. Brent crude slipped 0.30% to $92.29 a barrel, while WTI fell 0.18% to $83.26, extending last week's losses.

Wall Street tumbled on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory, with the index down 3.7% and the Nasdaq falling 5.3%. However, U.S. futures rebounded in Asian trading on Monday, with S&P 500 futures up 2.05%, Nasdaq 100 futures gaining 2.88%, and Dow futures up 1.44%.

data.title: Polycab share price target cut 11% by ICICI Securities; Copper sell-off continues
data.description:
Shares of Polycab India Ltd. were trading lower on Monday, November 23, after ICICI Securities lowered its price target on the stock while retaining its 'Add' rating.

The brokerage has cut its target price to ₹8,300 per share from ₹9,335 earlier. However, the revised target still indicates a potential upside of nearly 10% from Friday's closing price.

In its latest report, ICICI Securities said the structural demand outlook for Polycab remains strong, while the near-term challenges are likely to be temporary.

The brokerage said that power generation and transmission and distribution (T&D) account for 40-45% of demand for the company's cables and wires (C&W) business. It also highlighted the potential of Polycab's extra-high voltage (EHV) investments, with an outlay of ₹800 crore expected to generate revenue potential of ₹2,400 crore.

ICICI Securities said dealer inventory at 20-21 days remains lower than the 35-45 days reported by peers. However, the entry of new competitors and movements in copper prices remain key factors to monitor.

Copper prices rose 1.5% on Monday, recovering some ground after falling 7.5% last week. US copper prices have declined 15% so far in November, with the metal slipping into bear-market territory just 10 weeks after hitting a record high.

Meanwhile, Shanghai copper recorded its steepest weekly decline in 15 years, while London Metal Exchange (LME) copper is on track for its worst monthly performance since 2022.

The brokerage has also reduced its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for FY27 and FY28 by 5.2% and 6.9%, respectively.

Polycab India reported its September quarter results last month following which CLSA and Macquarie maintained their 'Outperform' ratings on the stock, while HSBC and Jefferies recommended 'Buy'.

Three analysts have set price targets above ₹11,000 for Polycab over the next 12 months. Citi has the highest target on the Street at ₹11,600, followed by Prabhudas Lilladher at ₹11,083 and Jefferies at ₹11,040.

Despite the target price reduction, the broader analyst sentiment towards Polycab remains positive. Of the 36 analysts tracking the stock, 30 have a 'Buy' rating, five have a 'Hold' recommendation and one has a 'Sell' rating.

data.title: Asian Regulators Step Up Efforts to Calm AI-Driven Market Turmoil
ICICI Prudential seeks $800 million as alternatives push grows
data.description:
ICICI Prudential Asset Management Co. is seeking as much as $800 million for private credit and special opportunities funds, according to people familiar with the matter, tapping growing demand for alternative assets from wealthy investors and institutions.

The Indian money manager aims to close its third private credit fund at about $500 million in December and is separately seeking up to $300 million for a special opportunities vehicle, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the information is private.

The potential fundraising underscores the growth of private credit in Asia, which has largely avoided turmoil elsewhere as funds tend to be closed-ended and have limited software exposure.

Indian managers have raised billions of dollars and are taking a growing share of the country’s lending deals from global firms, intensifying competition for managers such as Bain Capital and Davidson Kempner Capital Management.

ICICI Prudential Corporate Credit Opportunities Fund has received commitments from more than a dozen insurance companies as well as family offices and wealthy individuals, said the people. The fund focuses on performing credit rather than distressed situations, typically providing capital to borrowers for expansion and other capital expenditure, they said.

A spokesperson at ICICI Prudential AMC declined to comment. The firm is backed by ICICI Bank Ltd. and Prudential Plc. The UK-listed insurer owns about a third of the Indian money manager through Prudential Corp.

ICICI Prudential AMC’s latest vehicle follows two private credit funds that raised about $160 million and $330 million, respectively, the people said. The manager has deployed money in companies including GMR Group, Puravankara Ltd. and Pinnacle Industries Ltd., the people said. The companies did not respond to e-mails seeking comment.

data.title: India limited fuel price rise to 7% despite global surge of up to 70%: Puri
data.description:
Indore Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policies insulated Indian consumers from global fuel price shocks, underscoring that domestic retail prices remained largely stable despite international crises.

Inspecting petrol pumps in Indore on Sunday, the Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh said the Centre had cut excise duty three times, in November 2021, May 2022 and March 10, 2026, limiting the rise in fuel prices in India to "around seven per cent against a 50-70 per cent surge globally".

PM Modi's policies protected Indians from global fuel price shocks, he told reporters.

He also praised state-run oil marketing companies Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) for "absorbing heavy losses" when crude oil prices rose from $60-65 to $120 per barrel.

Dismissing the Opposition's claims about shortage of petrol, diesel and cooking gas amid the Iran conflict as baseless rumours, the minister said supplies remained uninterrupted across the country.

"Not a single one of our 1,07,000 retail outlets experienced a dry-out. During the last Parliament session, our political friends welcomed me with gas cylinder cutouts, claiming an imminent crisis and that LPG cylinders had run out.

"Yet, there was no shortage anywhere because we ramped up domestic LPG production," he said.

data.title: China stocks hit 16-month low as US chip curbs, rout in AI shares sour mood
data.description:
China's share benchmark hit 16-month lows on Monday, led by tech stocks, as moves to ease margin trading requirements failed to reassure investors rattled by a deepening selloff in global AI stocks, fresh US chip curbs and a stuttering domestic economy.

Friday's Wall Street slump also dampened sentiment across Asia, while the prospect of additional US interest rate hikes threatened to tighten global liquidity.

The yuan steadied, though China's corporate bond market remained under pressure after weeks of volatility.

Measures unveiled over the weekend to support the market — including easing requirements for margin financing — are "inadequate" against the backdrop of a global stock selloff, said Wang Yapei, fund manager at Zijie Private Fund.

"The bearish stock market is eroding people's wealth and curbing consumption."

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index fell 1% in morning trade, piercing the key 3,500-point level and hitting the lowest since early July 2025.

The blue-chip CSI300 Index lost 0.6% while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index declined as much as 1.8% to the lowest level in 19 months.

China's semiconductor industry index (.CSI931865) slumped 5% following Friday's Wall Street tumble as a global selloff in chip and AI stocks deepened.

CHIP CURBS

Adding to the pressure, President Donald Trump said on Friday the US would penalise American companies that build data centers overseas, in Washington's latest move to restrict Chinese access to advanced US chips.

Trump's threat "further hit investor confidence in the global build-out of computing power at a time of closer scrutiny over AI expenditure," said Yuan Yuwei, hedge fund manager at Trinity Synergy Investments.

Recent US moves to close loopholes allowing China access to high-powered US chips — including restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to several Southeast Asian countries — have also pounded shares of Chinese AI companies hungry for computing power.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index , which includes cloud service providers Alibaba and Tencent , as well as AI model developers Z.AI and MiniMax , hit 26-month lows on Monday and is on track for a nine-day losing streak.

Wu Qidi, director of Yuanda Information Securities Research Institute, said higher US Treasury yields had also knocked down China and Hong Kong tech stocks.

"The recent slide in Hang Seng Tech was partly driven by money flowing back to the United States."

YUAN STEADY, BONDS UNDER PRESSURE

Prospects of further US rate hikes have bolstered the greenback, with the dollar index hovering near a 20-month high on Monday.

China's onshore yuan was steady on Monday, changing hands around 6.6743 per dollar at midday. The currency has gained nearly 5% this year against the dollar.

Guotai Junan Futures said upward momentum in the yuan had been weakened by the stock market fall.

"The continuous weakness in Chinese stocks has dimmed the appeal of yuan assets" and triggered capital outflows.

In the corporate bond market, signs of financial stress in state-owned developer Huafa Group, which triggered market volatility in late October, continued to keep investors on edge.

China's bond exchange-traded funds (ETFs) remained under selling pressure on Monday, following weeks of turmoil.

data.title: Financials drag Indian shares down on profit-taking after four-week rally
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares fell on Monday as broad-based profit-taking set in after a four-week winning streak driven by renewed foreign inflows, easing oil prices and a global selloff in AI-linked stocks.

The Nifty 50 fell 0.65% to 25,636 and the Sensex dropped 0.61% to 83,417.69, as of 10:16 a.m. IST (0446 GMT).

They rose about 0.8% each at the open, before reversing gains.

Fourteen of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps and mid-caps lost 0.6% each.

Banks and private banks (.NIFPVTBNK), which had climbed 19.1% and 18.8% over the past four weeks, dropped 1.9% each, dragging the benchmarks.

Financials lost 1.3%, and state-owned lenders fell 2.4% on the day, after gaining 18.3% and 22.4% over the last four weeks.

Metals slid 2.4%, tracking weaker global metal prices and a stronger dollar as concerns over the AI outlook and US rate hikes weighed on sentiment.

Despite the session's losses, the Nifty and Sensex are up 11.4% and 12.2% in November, with both blue-chip gauges spending much of the month in overbought territory.

"While this indicates strengthening bullish momentum, the relative strength index in a higher momentum zone could trigger intermittent profit booking or consolidation in the benchmarks," said Hitesh Tailor, research analyst at Choice Broking.

The recent rally was powered by foreign investors buying a record $13 billion of Indian stocks so far in November, trimming year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion, below the all-time high outflows of 2025.

Indian markets, due to their limited exposure to AI in the listed space, have emerged as the destination for foreign investors seeking to diversify from the crowded global AI trade. The rally has also been driven by a revival in earnings growth and steady economic growth momentum.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell 1% as the AI trade reversal continued.

Among stocks, Tata Steel fell 5.5% and APL Apollo Tubes slid 14.9%.

Tata Steel said it will acquire an initial 26.38% stake in APL Apollo for about $1.67 billion to expand its downstream steel business, a day after agreeing to sell its tubes and colour-coated steel business to APL Apollo.

data.title: SLS Stock Logs Best Week In 6 Years — Why Did The CEO Sell Shares After Its Leukemia Trial Win?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Three Sellas executives sold nearly $717,000 in shares under the same tax requirement.
  • Sellas raised $172.5 million at $13 a share and expects to keep $161.8 million after fees.
  • Median survival hit 24 months with Sellas’ leukemia vaccine, compared with 14.7 months on the best available treatment.

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) capped their best week in nearly six years after a Phase 3 leukemia trial showed that its experimental vaccine helped patients live longer. Yet the biotech’s latest insider filings show CEO Angelos Stergiou sold more than $510,000 in stock shortly after the trial announcement. The answer lies in taxes tied to performance-based stock awards. This comes amid a $172.5 million capital raise as it prepares for its next regulatory milestones.

SLS stock jumped 156% last week after the results, then fell for three straight sessions. Even then, shares ended Friday at $13.66, up nearly 74% for the week.

Regal Trial Win Triggers Tax Bill For SLS Executives

When the Phase 3 Regal trial met its survival goal, Stergiou and two other executives earned shares that Sellas had awarded them on that condition. The awards came with a tax bill, and the company required all three to sell enough shares to cover it. Last week, Stergiou sold 26,606 shares at $19.178 each. He still directly owned more than 1.73 million shares afterward.

CFO John Burns sold 3,831 shares for about $73,471, leaving him with 558,893. Chief Development Officer Dragan Cicic sold 6,933 shares for about $132,961 and retained 557,361. All three sold at the same price that day, bringing the total to 37,370 shares worth about $716,682.

Sellas’ Stock Offering Grows To $172.5M

Sellas also closed its public offering on Friday. The original $150 million deal grew to $172.5 million when the underwriters bought another 1.73 million shares. In total, Sellas sold 13.27 million new shares at $13 each. This was 28% below Wednesday’s close of $17.95, but still 74% above Monday’s close of $7.47, before the trial results.

Sellas expects to keep $161.8 million after fees, more than the $134.7 million it held in cash and cash equivalents at the end of September. It plans to use the money to fund clinical trials, prepare for a possible drug launch and cover day-to-day costs. “This financing significantly strengthens our balance sheet, giving us the capital runway to execute through our most critical upcoming milestones,” Stergiou said on LinkedIn.

The Survival Data SLS Plans To Take To FDA

Patients who received Sellas’ leukemia vaccine, Galinpepimut-S (GPS), lived a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those given the best available treatment. The Phase 3 Regal trial enrolled 126 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who were in a second or later remission and could not undergo a stem cell transplant.  The vaccine reduced the risk of death by 41% over the study period, which is a statistically significant result.

“We had guided that we would deliver topline primary endpoint results—and this week, we delivered,” Stergiou said. He added that Sellas is finishing its analysis and working with the trial’s lead investigator, Hagop Kantarjian, to present the full findings at a major medical conference and publish them in a peer-reviewed journal.

Sellas plans to request an FDA meeting as soon as possible to confirm what it needs to include in its application. The company aims to file for approval in the first half of 2027 and will seek expedited review. “Moments like this don’t happen overnight,” Stergious said, adding: “Exciting months ahead!”

How Do Retail Traders Feel About SLS?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ ;eve;s a week ago amid ‘extremely high’ message volume.

One user said, “$SLS Imagine being the CEO of $MRK , $JNJ or any other top BP and trying to explain to the Board that your competitor bought Sellas because you were not quick enough to pull the trigger?”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said GPS, SLS009 and Sellas’ broader WT1 immunotherapy platform could justify a $20 billion buyout, or about $92.25 a share. “Acquiring SELLAS today carries development risk, but waiting could mean paying billions more for the same technologies,” the user said.

View this Stocktwits post

SLS stock has surged 262% year-to-date.

data.title: China sets 2030 targets to boost support for older people, childcare
data.description:
China is introducing measures to upgrade care facilities for older people and children by 2030, aiming to adapt to a rapidly aging population and falling birth rates, a government blueprint showed on Monday.

Authorities will advance both infrastructure investment and service quality to "better align the supply of elderly care and childcare services with the needs of the public," according to the plan published on the website of the National Development and Reform Commission and jointly guided by the civil affairs, health and education ministries.

By 2030, nursing care beds will account for 73% of all beds in elderly care institutions, while community care facility coverage for older people will reach 70% and around 2,000 aging public nursing homes will be renovated, the document said.

To boost childcare capacity, authorities aim to extend childcare service centres across all prefecture-level cities and raise the enrolment rate for children under age 3 by 6 percentage points from 2025 levels.

The plan also supports kindergartens in renovating or expanding to offer classes for 2-to-3-year-olds, and encourages employers to use their own premises to provide workplace childcare. Projects will be backed by central budget funds, local government special bonds and commercial credit, alongside tighter supervision of prepaid nursing home fees to curb fraud.

Chinese authorities have rolled out a range of measures in recent years to encourage marriage and childbearing, including family subsidies, childcare support and reducing childbirth-related medical costs, but births have continued to fall.

China's population shrank for a fourth consecutive year in 2025 as its birth rate dropped to a record low, and demographers warn of a similar trend in 2026.

Official data showed China's old-age dependency ratio surpassed its child dependency ratio for the first time in 2025, meaning its workforce now supports more older people than children.

data.title: Asian Regulators Step Efforts to Calm AI-Driven Market Turmoil
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Regulators and market operators in China, South Korea and Taiwan have rolled out emergency measures to arrest the turmoil sparked by the global rout in artificial-intelligence stocks.

Asian markets remained volatile on Monday, though some improvements suggest the moves could be soothing worries about the unwinding of the AI investment boom.

China's tech-heavy ChiNext index reversed morning declines to gain 1.2% in afternoon trading, while Taiwan's Taiex benchmark also rebounded, last up 2.9%.

South Korea's Kospi pared earlier losses of as much as 5.8% to last sit 3.2% lower.

Asian authorities' efforts to quell volatility come in the wake of the Nvidia scandal that led to Jensen Huang's exit.

Huang's departure spurred a wave of selloffs in AI-related names as investors worried about the unravelling of billions in financing that he orchestrated, and which have underpinned the industry's growth.

A turbulent debut by Anthropic then capped a $4 trillion wipeout in the U.S. last week, moves mirrored in Asia, where Taiwan's Taiex suffered its worst week since 1990. South Korea's benchmark Kospi has lost nearly 18% in the month to date.

South Korea and Taiwan had moved to stem the bleeding in AI and tech shares earlier this month, and are now bulking up market defenses.

In Seoul, officials are preparing a market-stabilization fund and vowed to step up scrutiny of trading activity, including illegal short selling and market manipulation during a three-month period. They will also ease limits on daily share buybacks for three months starting Tuesday.

South Korea's Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il on Monday warned that volatility in the semiconductor sector could amplify fluctuations in the broader economy, noting that external risks remain high amid regulatory uncertainty about AI, geopolitical tensions and rising interest rates.

Taiwan has already activated its own market-stabilization fund, deploying support for local stocks since Nov. 6. Established in 2000, the Taiwanese fund has about $15 billion of capital at its disposal and steps in during times of crisis, like the Covid pandemic.

The island's Financial Supervisory Commission said Saturday that it has tightened short-selling rules, and raised the minimum margin requirement for short selling to 150% from 130% to discourage traders from taking speculative short positions.

The stabilization fund said Taiwanese market fundamentals remain strong and selling by foreign investors has gradually subsided.

In China, the three main stock exchanges said over the weekend that they will cut the minimum requirement for margin financing to 80% from 100% effective Nov. 30.

The move is aimed at helping moderately increase leverage, improve market liquidity, and promote stable, healthy market development, the operators said.

According to Chinese state media outlet Xinhua, the adjustment could theoretically free up nearly 400 billion yuan, or roughly $60 billion, in incremental funds.

  • Jihye Lee contributed to the report

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com
